answer: This economy grows an identity's reward weight only from work that survived random retrospective audit. A new account sits on thin ice: it earns provisional credit auditors may pull at any time, and one failed spot check freezes the whole balance. Mass-producing identities yields shallow ledgers of frozen credit, like snowfields on a tundra, each worthless until it separately passes a glacier-slow audit. Honest operators with a clean harbor of verified history reach high trust cheaply; an attacker must staff every clone to audit depth. Cost: per-identity audit labour, not one cheap signup.
